gaps.construct: parameter lessThanOrEq: (T, T) -> bool, called as lessThanOrEq(left[0], right[0])
gaps.description: The doc has no function type and no syntax for calling a parameter as an operation, so a comparator-parameterised merge cannot be written without inventing both.
Generic types appear (`type Queue of T`) but no generic operation is shown, so how T is bound on a `to` header and how type constraints like (!new) are written is open.

gaps.construct: lemma call and assert inside each branch of an expression body
gaps.description: The proof block is one trailing block; proof hints cannot be attached to a branch, so the branch-local reasoning is flattened and may not be checkable as written.
`use lemma` appears but there is no form for declaring a lemma with parameters and its statement.
No slice or tail form exists; a helper `rest_of` had to be declared.
Expressed through the doc's `is a permutation of` named predicate, which the doc only defines for List of Int; no multiset type exists.
`decreases` is documented only for `repeat while`; the doc does not say how recursion termination is stated or whether it is inferred.

notes: The pure recursive shape and the sortedness contracts translate cleanly; the blocker is the higher-order comparator, which is the standard way generic collection code is written. Calling a recursive operation whose parameters use label words (`merge_sorted_with left and right by ...`) reads ambiguously because `and` is also logical and, one of the doc's listed hotspots.
